a. And these are the matters concerning his lineage; the plot of the Argonautica of Apollonius is as follows.

Tyro, daughter of Salmoneus and Alcidice, bore to Poseidon Neleus and Pelias. Then she married Cretheus, son of Aeolus, and bore to him Aeson, Pheres, and Amythaon. And from Aeson was born Jason, from Pheres Admetus, and from Amythaon Melampus. And Jason was given to Chiron to be raised and to learn medicine, since his father Aeson had left his own kingdom to his brother Pelias and ordered him to rule and govern Thessaly, until

Jason will return from Chiron. Pelias had received an oracle from Apollo to beware of the one-sandaled man who would come to him; for he would die because of him. Jason, having grown up, went to his father's brothers, intending to share in his father's kingdom. When he came to the river Anaurus—this is in Thessaly—and wished to cross, he found on the bank Hera disguised as an old woman, wanting to cross but afraid, and standing there, as he says (III 72), like an old woman. Then Jason, recognizing this, took her on his shoulders and carried her across, leaving one sandal in the mud in the middle of the river. Then he went to the city with one sandal and found a public festival and sacrifice being held to the gods by Pelias. Seeing Jason with one sandal, Pelias remembered the oracle. Being cautious about killing him, he assigned him such a contest, saying: "Go to Scythia and bring back the golden fleece, and you will receive your father's kingdom." He assigned this not because he needed the golden fleece, but thinking that Jason would be killed by someone in a foreign land or would be shipwrecked at sea. LGP
